new_evidence.observation: Official match pages visibly publish team-level expected-goals totals for at least sampled 2024, 2025 and 2026 J1 fixtures.
new_evidence.reason: This corrects the earlier shorthand that the official site was identity/format-only. It proves genuine J.League xG exists, but does not establish an open licence permitting systematic archival/reuse, a stable no-login machine dataset, immutable content identity/available_at, or complete 2022-2025 match-level coverage. No systematic scrape is performed.

new_evidence.observation: Official 2022 statistics prove xG was produced historically, but season/player aggregate pages are not match-level home_xg/away_xg rows.

new_evidence.source: Hudl StatsBomb free Japan 2024 J1 release
new_evidence.observation: Free event data exists for Japan 2024 J1 and StatsBomb event data can carry shot-level xG.
new_evidence.reason: J1 only and one season; the frozen gate requires 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 historical seasons and K1 remains uncovered.

new_evidence.observation: K League officially publishes xG analyses from 2022 onward and identifies Bepro data in current xG reporting.
new_evidence.reason: The public evidence establishes genuine K League xG production, but not a no-key, no-login, licence-acceptable multi-season match-level home_xg/away_xg archive with stable kickoff and observed/available provenance.

new_evidence.source: FootyStats J1/K League 1 datasets and API
new_evidence.observation: The service advertises multi-season J1/K1 xG and match datasets, but programmatic access is directed to a subscription API with an API key.
